title: Nvidia board got 'input from senior levels' of US government
excerpt: Nvidia wrote that, "based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk."
content_html:
Trump says his input was 'very important' in bringing Jensen Huang back to Nvidia

By Natalie Musumeci

You're currently following this author! Click to unsubscribe from email alerts.

and Thibault Spirlet

You're currently following this author! Click to unsubscribe from email alerts.

2026-11-23T16:26:46.266Z

President Donald Trump said he worked behind the scenes to help secure Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO and said the board ultimately followed the administration's preferred course.

"I was talking to a lot of people" about Huang's return, Trump told CNBC on Monday. "The board decided to do what we wanted them to do."

Trump said he spoke to Huang the night before Nvidia's shock announcement because he knew "what was going on," and said he urged the Nvidia founder to return.

"I've been speaking to the board directly and indirectly, and I felt very strongly about it," Trump added.

Trump made the comments shortly after Nvidia said that it had reinstated Huang, less than two weeks after he resigned amid an affair scandal and an investigation into whether he had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort.

Nvidia said its board had received input from "senior levels" of the US government before unanimously restoring Huang. The company said it was confident that his return "poses no national security risk."

Trump said the US had conducted "thorough investigations" and called Huang a "national treasure," arguing that the greater threat to US national security would be losing the AI-chip executive to China.

"The threat is to lose him," Trump said.

Huang's return comes after Trump and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent signaled their support for Huang's return to the chip giant over the weekend.

A day before the bombshell announcement, Trump wrote in a Truth Social post: "I hope the Board of Nvidia rehires Jensen Huang." The president said it would be best for the company and the US.

Bessent, who initially said Nvidia's board should consider candidates "outside the company" to replace Huang, later suggested Huang could fit that description himself.

"I said they should go to the outside, but he's on the outside now," Bessent said in an interview Sunday.

Others, including Nvidia employees, investors, and prominent tech leaders like Elon Musk, had also rallied for Huang's return to the company he founded more than 30 years ago.

Earlier this month, Huang admitted to being "unfaithful" to his wife after The New York Times reported that he had developed a close relationship with Alice Huang, a former top executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company and major buyer of Nvidia chips.

The report said American officials had concluded that Alice Huang was a Chinese intelligence asset gathering information for Beijing — an accusation China has repeatedly denied.

On the day of Jensen Huang's admission, Nvidia's board said it was launching an independent investigation into whether he was the target of a foreign intelligence effort.

Four days later, Jensen Huang resigned following a report that he also had an extramarital affair with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare and a direct report.

Nvidia's board said Monday that it "voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang's candor and ability to lead NVIDIA."

Harvey C. Jones, the board chair, said in a statement that Jensen Huang's return is in the "best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers."

Shortly after the news, Trump weighed in in another Truth Social post, saying Nvidia's board "made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO."

"The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security," Trump said.

Trump added that he had gotten to know Huang on a personal level, and called him a "Great Patriot and National Treasure."

Nvidia's board said Monday that it "voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang's candor and ability to lead NVIDIA."

Harvey C. Jones, the board chair, said in a statement that Jensen Huang's return is in the "best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers."

Shortly after the news, Trump weighed in in another Truth Social post, saying Nvidia's board "made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO."

"The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security," Trump said.

Trump added that he had gotten to know Huang on a personal level, and called him a "Great Patriot and National Treasure."
